subject: Activation readiness: lane owners, gating windows, and enablement plan
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2024-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Activation readiness: lane owners, gating windows, and enablement plan

Team —

We need to lock a few things ahead of the April activation window. Quick ask: can each functional owner confirm the lane-level decisions below by EOD tomorrow so I can finalize the kickoff for Sales + CS next week? High-level items: 

- Gating windows (hard start / soft launch / canary % and duration) per lane (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Final document owners for enablement artifacts (playbook, runbooks, troubleshooting checklist).
- Any exception lanes where we allow extended beta (and who owns approvals).
- Training slots for CS and Sales (we have two 60-min slots available 04/17 & 04/19).

I attached a first-pass enablement playbook and a canary matrix. If you can annotate the matrix with your preferred canary % and fallback triggers, that would be ideal.

Notes: we should default to the conservative gating plan (10% for hosted, 5% for dedicated, 2% for private) unless owners push back with a reasoned rollback/fallback path.

Thanks — Vivek
--
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2024-04-11T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Activation readiness: lane owners, gating windows, and enablement plan

Vivek —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick responses from my lane (Enablement / Docs):

- Document ownership: Enablement playbook -> Marissa Cole (I will shepherd); Runbooks -> Marcus Lin (ops) as primary, with Priyom as secondary for triage flows.
- Gating windows: I agree with conservative defaults as baseline. For hosted, suggest 10% x 72 hours with automated rollback on error-rate > 3% or lat > 750ms P95.
- Exceptions: we have one enterprise customer (Acme) flagged for an extended pilot — Grace can confirm SLA exceptions; Marissa to own the exception checklist.
- Training: take the 04/17 slot for a walk-through (Sales + Solutions) and 04/19 for hands-on sessions with CS and Customer Success Managers.

Action items I will do today: annotate the attached playbook with content owners, add a short decision flow for exceptions, and update the Drive link.

Attachment: enablement_playbook_v1.pdf (see section 3.2 for the exception checklist)

-Marissa
--
Marissa Cole
Director, Developer Marketing & Enablement
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2024-04-11T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Activation readiness: lane owners, gating windows, and enablement plan

Quick infra/ops context from my side:

- Runbooks: I will publish the troubleshooting runbook (runbook_v1) by EOD. Priyom will own the rollback runbook and smoke-test checklist.
- Canary details: suggested canary -> hosted 8-12% (target 10%), dedicated 5% fixed for 48h, private 1-3% (target 2%) with manual approval for >2%.
- Fallback triggers: error-rate > 2.5% (5xxs) or token-generation latency P95 > 900ms or KV cache miss rate spike > 10%.
- Ops readiness: we will have an on-call rotation for the first 72h post-canary (Marcus, Priyom, ops-oncall). I'll add the rotation to the runbook.

Also flagged: we need a short FAQ for SEs on "what to tell customers" if we hit a canary rollback. Marissa — can you add a 2-paragraph customer-facing blurb in the playbook?

-Marcus
--
Marcus Lin
Head of Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2024-04-11T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Activation readiness: lane owners, gating windows, and enablement plan

Ack —

I'll own the rollback checklist and the smoke test automation. Tentatively allocating the 04/19 10:00-11:00 PT slot for CS hands-on (booking link to follow).

Two quick notes: 
1) For the private lane, customers that require key management integration need an extra security checklist step (KMS/HSM validation). Marcus — can you add a KMS smoke check?
2) I'll add the on-call rota in the runbook and include a short escalation path with pager duty snippets.

-Priyom

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2024-04-11T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Activation readiness: lane owners, gating windows, and enablement plan

Thanks all — this is exactly the level of specificity I needed. Summary / decisions: 

- Owners: Enablement playbook = Marissa; Runbooks + rollback = Marcus (primary) / Priyom (secondary).
- Canary plan: hosted 10% x 72h, dedicated 5% x 48h, private 2% x 72h (manual approval for >2%). Fallback triggers as Marcus outlined.
- Exceptions: Acme pilot approved for extended beta; Grace to own customer-level exceptions and sign-off checklist.
- Training: Sales walk-through 04/17; CS hands-on 04/19 (Priyom to send invites).
- Deliverables: Marissa to update playbook and add customer-facing FAQ; Marcus/Priyom to publish runbooks and rota. Share final docs in Drive by EOD 04/12.

I'll send the consolidated kickoff invite for Sales+CS tomorrow morning once the Drive links are updated.

Vivek
--
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
